problem: Given $P(A)=\frac{1}{4},$ $P(B)=\frac{3}{10},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{19}{40},$ determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
worked_solution:
To check if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, we must check that $P(A\cap B)=0.$

We can calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{19}{40} & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{10}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{10}-\frac{19}{40} \\  & =\frac{10+12-19}{40} \\  & =\frac{3}{40} \\  & \ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events.
